c.tagline: Geysers, hot springs and living Māori culture on the shores of a caldera lake.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are metered; Uber and Ola operate but with limited driver numbers, so waits can be longer than in the big cities. Door-to-door airport shuttles are a cheaper option, especially for two or more people.

emergency.note: 111 is New Zealand's single emergency number for police, fire and ambulance.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: The city centre can feel empty late at night, and thefts from parked cars at trailheads and geothermal car parks do occur — leave nothing visible.

hood_desc: The compact town centre around Tutanekai Street and the covered Eat Streat dining lane, walkable to shops, cafes, bars and tour operators; the easiest base for first-timers without a car.
The reserve along the southern shore of Lake Rotorua, home to the Government Gardens, Rotorua Museum, Blue Baths and the jetty for lake cruises; scenic and central to the top sights.
A historic, still-lived-in Māori lakeside village with the carved St Faith's Church and free steaming geothermal vents; a quieter, budget-friendly and culturally rich place to stay.
The main accommodation corridor running south from the CBD toward Whakarewarewa, packed with motels, holiday parks and mid-range hotels close to the geothermal attractions.
The geothermal heart on the town's southern edge, home to Te Puia's Pōhutu Geyser and the Living Māori Village; a sightseeing base wrapped in steam, mud pools and forest.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink; the sulphur smell in town comes from geothermal air, not the water.

transit.hours: Baybus services run roughly 7am to 6pm on weekdays with reduced weekend timetables; there is no late-night network, so taxis, rideshare or shuttles cover the evenings.
transit.note: Rotorua has no rail or tram; the Baybus / Cityride network of local buses links the CBD with the suburbs, the airport (Route 10) and geothermal attractions, supplemented by shuttles, taxis and rideshare.
transit.pay: Fares are paid with a Bee Card (tap on/off, sold and topped up at agents or online) or in cash to the driver; the Bee Card is cheaper per trip.

transit.m: Baybus Route 10 to the city centre (~20 min, roughly half-hourly on weekdays)
Door-to-door shuttle to city hotels, ~15 min

tip.r: Tipping is not expected in New Zealand; service is included and rounding up for exceptional service is entirely optional.
